title: Verify pytest collection includes the intended regression files
applies_when: A Python repository adds tests under a different filename convention, or a green directory run is being used to qualify a change in a supposedly included module.
lesson: Read the effective pytest configuration and actual collected case identities before interpreting a green suite. At the cited Voluptuous revision, python_files='tests.py' excludes test_dataclasses.py from the directory command used by tox, although that file passes when selected alone. Existing PR #555 explicitly acknowledges the omission and places its regressions in the collected file; do not rediscover its Optional repair. Require at least one intended case from each relevant test file, not only an unrelated passing sentinel or aggregate count. A directory-plus-file argument list is not itself collection proof: inspect the resulting report. If a deliberately expanded selection is needed, declare it separately, keep identical test bytes/configuration in both arms, and retain the original missing-case result.
avoid_when: A missing case is not a failed assertion, evidence that the tests are broken, or permission to rewrite reports or silently relax required identities. A later expanded run does not retroactively qualify the earlier selection. Correct collection does not establish imported production identity, test quality, all optional dependencies, CI approval, maintainer acceptance, or measured Scout accuracy/cost improvement. Do not change a project's import mode or skip tests merely to get a green report.

evidence.note: Pinned pytest configuration sets python_files='tests.py' and testpaths to voluptuous/tests. This is collection-mechanism evidence, not a full-suite local pass.
The Python tox command selects the test directory, so the effective filename pattern matters.

Existing author's report distinguishes the normal 190-case selection from 19 explicitly invoked dataclass tests and places eight new cases in the normally collected file. This is prior author-owned work, not our new Optional finding or endorsement of its entire fix.
Official pytest documentation describes filename/class/function collection conventions and checking collected tests. Check the actual installed version and resulting identities.
